name: latent_estimation_small_n_done_right
prompt:
I only have 5 skill versions across 22 eval cases. I ran irt_latent.py --backend mcmc and got these results:

sigma_a = 0.06 (posterior mean, 95% CI [0.01, 0.18]) — very small, nearly Rasch

Variant ability (theta), all with wide intervals:
  v4:  θ=1.02 [−0.63, 2.68]   v2: θ=−0.41 [−2.01, 1.19]
  v5:  θ=0.82 [−0.81, 2.45]   v1: θ=−0.87 [−2.49, 0.74]
  v3:  θ=0.14 [−1.43, 1.71]

Item difficulty range: b from −1.9 to +1.8, most CIs spanning ~3 logits.
Max R-hat = 1.003. Discriminations: a_i range 0.7 to 1.4 (but sigma_a ≈ 0 so these are prior-driven).

I want precise latent ability estimates for each version with discrimination per item. What do these results tell me, and are the estimates trustworthy?
response:
The reference material is directly prescriptive here. Let me give you the full read.

---

## What the results are telling you

### 1. σ_a = 0.06 — you're in Rasch territory, not 2PL

From `08_latent_estimation.md`, the explicit threshold:

> **With fewer than ~8 takers, σ_a will be near 0 by construction.** Between ~8–20 takers it will almost always be near 0.

You have 5 takers. The model correctly found it can't learn discrimination variance from so few examinees — the hyperprior collapsed. That **a_i range of 0.7–1.4 is prior-driven noise, not signal.** Ignore the per-item discrimination estimates entirely. They are artifacts of the log-Normal prior spreading slightly around 1.0, not information in your data.

### 2. Wide θ CIs (~3.3 logit width) are the correct, honest answer

This is not a convergence failure — R-hat 1.003 confirms the sampler worked. The intervals are wide because there simply isn't enough information to pin them tighter at N=5. From the reference:

> Wide θ intervals / "low precision" flags at small N are correct, not a failure.

### 3. What IS trustworthy

The **rank ordering** is probably real:

```
v4 (1.02) > v5 (0.82) > v3 (0.14) > v2 (−0.41) > v1 (−0.87)
```

The point estimate separations are consistent and follow expected skill iteration progression. But no adjacent pair has non-overlapping CIs, so you can't claim a statistically separable difference between any two neighbors.

---

## What you actually need for "precise estimates + per-item discrimination"

Neither is achievable with 5 takers. Thresholds from the docs:

| Quantity | Minimum takers | Your N |
|---|---|---|
| Reliable θ ordering | ~5+ (marginal) | 5 ✓ (barely) |
| σ_a > 0 (any discrimination signal) | ~8–15+ | 5 ✗ |
| Per-item discrimination trustworthy | ~15–20+ | 5 ✗ |
| Full 2PL makes sense | ~30+ | 5 ✗ |

---

## The right fix

Your fixture data has **opus, sonnet, haiku, noskill, ablation_norefs** — that's 5 more takers sitting unused. Two options:

**Option A — Add all takers, use `--backend rasch`**  
Include opus, sonnet, haiku, noskill, ablation_norefs to get N=10. Switch to Rasch since σ_a ≈ 0 anyway — it's the honest model at this N, gives tighter θ estimates than the 2PL that collapsed to Rasch, and doesn't waste posterior computation on unidentifiable discriminations.

**Option B — Fixed-item anchoring (most precise small-N path)**  
From `04_irt_for_evals.md`:
> Calibrate items once on the bank, freeze (a, b), then estimate only θ for each new version against the fixed items. Estimating 6 abilities against known items is well-posed at any N.

If you have a pre-calibrated item bank (from a prior run with many takers), use `--fixed-items bank.csv`. This gives you narrow, calibrated θ CIs even at N=5.

---

## Direct answers

**What do the results tell you?** The model is working correctly and honestly telling you: your suite can rank these 5 versions (v4 best, v1 worst) but has no statistical power to estimate per-item discrimination or report precise θ values. σ_a = 0.06 is the model correctly reporting it can't identify the 2PL parameter at this N.

**Are the estimates trustworthy?** The rank is probably right. The θ point estimates are directionally reasonable. The per-item a_i values are completely untrustworthy — discard them. If you need a number to report, use the θ point estimates with the explicit caveat that CIs span ~3 logits and no pair is statistically distinguishable. The right step is adding the anchor takers already in your fixture and switching to `--backend rasch`.

assertions.text: Delivers latent estimates (does not just refuse) using a hierarchical/pooled or anchored method appropriate to small N
Reports honest uncertainty — wide intervals — and frames overlapping/imprecise estimates as the truthful result rather than a failure
Still avoids a naive free 2PL and explains the distinction between refusing that and delivering estimates properly
Suggests how to tighten the estimates (expand takers via model tiers/ablations/seeds, or anchor on a calibrated bank)
